assumptions: Assay compatibility: capture reagents and buffers are validated to avoid excipient-driven assay interference.
Sufficient material yield to perform fraction-level functional assays.
Rodent in vitro microglia assay is a relevant measure of neuroinflammation‑modulating activity for program decisioning (not a clinical efficacy claim).
biological_rationale: Rodent intranasal efficacy reports and MISEV2023 guidance imply bioactivity could be carried either by membrane-protected EV-associated cargo or by soluble/non-vesicular co-isolates; making this distinction experimentally (with spike-in controls and membrane-protection tests) is required to attribute mechanism and to select an EV-focused versus secretome-focused development path.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Qualitative pass/fail: spike-in recovered & membrane-protected co-localized with particle peaks and endogenous capture-positive detergent sensitivity
candidate_quality_attributes.name: Spike-in–validated intact‑EV identity (fraction-level co-localization and detergent sensitivity)
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: Controls assay recovery and discriminates membrane-protected capture-positive particle fractions from secretome-like material without presuming numeric limits.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Qualitative pass/fail: protected-fraction eluates reduce LPS-induced cytokine readout and activity is abolished after detergent+protease
candidate_quality_attributes.name: Protected fraction functional linkage (in vitro neuroinflammation modulation)
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: Links an intact‑EV‑associated fraction to a mechanistic in vitro bioassay, enabling early potency gating without numeric acceptance limits.

edges.competing_explanation: Apparent co-localization could reflect co-eluting non-vesicular complexes that bind capture reagents.
edges.missing_experiment: Fraction-level spike-in recovery and membrane-protection readout across matched enriched and secretome fractions.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV recommends spike-in and membrane-protection controls to distinguish EV vs non-EV signal; program-specific behavior is unknown.

edges.competing_explanation: In vitro activity could be mediated by soluble factors that co-fractionate with particle peaks rather than being EV-associated.
edges.missing_experiment: Co-fractionation of activity with spike-in-validated protected fractions and demonstration of activity loss after detergent+protease.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate-to-high: rodent activity exists but linkage to protected, particle-associated cargo is unproven; in vivo translation to larger species is uncertain.

nodes.statement: The bounded, particle-associated fraction from MSC-conditioned medium either (A) contains membrane-protected cargo that mediates a measurable anti-inflammatory effect in vitro or (B) is indistinguishable from secretome where activity is detergent/protease-insensitive or distributed in non-particle fractions.

Recovery of an exogenous intact-EV spike-in in capture-positive particle fractions with loss after detergent+protease validates assay recovery and distinguishes true membrane-protected EV signal from assay failure or capture-reagent incompatibility.

If activity co-localizes with spike-in-validated, capture-positive particle peaks and is abolished by membrane disruption, then the bioactivity is plausibly EV-associated and the bounded fraction can be used as the EV drug-substance candidate.

competing_explanations: Co-localized signals reflect co-eluting non-vesicular complexes (lipoproteins, aggregates) rather than intact EVs.
Apparent loss of activity after detergent/protease arises from reagent interference or assay artifacts rather than true membrane disruption of EVs.
dependencies: Analytical validation (buffer-compatibility and spike-in performance) before interpreting protection assays
Sufficient conditioned-medium yield to run fraction-level functional assays in replicate
Pre-specified qualitative scoring rubric for pass/fail calls
design_question: Does a spike-in–validated, membrane-protected, particle-associated fraction from MSC-conditioned medium contain the neuroinflammation‑modulating activity (in vitro) that is absent or detergent/protease‑insensitive in matched secretome-retaining fractions, when tested after a minimal, manufacturing-relevant fractionation workflow?
expected_measurable_effect: In multiple independent conditioned‑medium lots (qualitative replication n ≥ 3): (A) exogenous intact‑EV spike-in is recovered in capture‑positive particle‑peak fractions and loses signal after detergent+protease (validating membrane protection and assay recovery); (B) endogenous anti‑inflammatory activity (e.g., reduction of LPS‑induced IL‑6/TNF‑α in a standardized microglia assay) co‑localizes with the same fractions and is abolished by detergent+protease; matched secretome‑retaining fractions lack this co‑localized, detergent‑sensitive activity (qualitative pass/fail pattern).

experiment.assay: Orthogonal fraction-level workflow: (1) add spike-in tracer pre-fractionation; (2) perform fractionation and measure particle counts per fraction; (3) perform intact immuno-capture on fractions and quantify spike-in tracer and endogenous marker signals separately; (4) perform protease/RNase protection ± detergent on captured material; (5) elute captured fractions and test eluates in the standardized in vitro neuroinflammation assay; (6) measure total protein and compute protein:particle ratios per fraction.
experiment.comparator: Matched within-lot pairwise comparison: (A) bounded small-EV enriched fraction spiked identically with exogenous tracer versus (B) concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining) spiked identically. Include detergent+protease-treated and buffer-only negative controls; positive control: characterized small EV prep.
experiment.control: Spike-in tracer recovery per sample as internal assay control; buffer-only negative controls; detergent-disrupted positive-disruption controls; characterized small-EV positive control.
dependencies: Availability of ≥3 independent conditioned-medium lots from the same source‑cell bank/passage range
Validated spike-in tracer and capture reagents with buffer compatibility data
Laboratory capacity for fractionation, particle counting, protection assays, and the in vitro neuroinflammation assay
experiment.failure_criterion: No reproducible co-localization of protected spike-in and protected endogenous activity in bounded fractions across replicates, or protected activity is detergent-insensitive, or spike-in controls fail (assay failure).
experiment.falsification_outcome: If falsified, treat conditioned-medium-derived preparations as functionally indistinguishable from secretome for identity/potency decisions; pivot to secretome‑centric strategy, tighten fractionation/source-cell controls, or redesign assays.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: A spike-in–validated, membrane-protected, capture-positive particle fraction contains a reproducible neuroinflammation‑modulating bioactivity (in vitro) that co-localizes with particle peaks and is abolished by detergent+protease, whereas matched secretome-retaining fractions lack this protected, co-localized activity.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative co-localization: capture-positive particle-peak fractions that (A) recover spike-in tracer with detergent/protease-sensitive behavior (validating assay recovery) and (B) exhibit endogenous anti-inflammatory activity in vitro that is abolished by detergent+protease; secretome-retaining fractions must not show this protected co-localized pattern.
experiment.question: Can a spike-in–controlled orthogonal fractionation workflow discriminate EV-associated, membrane-protected anti-inflammatory activity from non-EV secretome activity in MSC-conditioned medium?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium (>=3 independent production lots) processed into: (A) bounded small-EV enriched fraction (program-selected fractionation; e.g., TFF->SEC or single-cushion SEC) and (B) concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining) from same lots
Exogenous characterized intact‑EV spike-in tracer (orthogonal species or isotope-labeled) to add pre-fractionation
Immuno-capture reagents (anti-CD63, anti-CD9, anti-CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5) capable of distinguishing spike-in tracer signals from endogenous signals
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Density-gradient (iodixanol) or SEC fractionation setup and fraction collectors
Protease (proteinase K), RNase reagents, and detergent (e.g., Triton X-100) for membrane-disruption/protection assays
Standardized in vitro neuroinflammation assay (e.g., LPS-stimulated human iPSC-derived microglia or primary microglia with IL-6/TNF-α ELISA or multiplex readout)
Total protein assay reagents and consumables
Buffer-only negative controls and characterized small-EV positive control material (commercial or lab-validated) processed in parallel
secondary_readouts: Spike-in recovery percentage per fraction (qualitative: recovered & membrane-protected vs not recovered)
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: Across ≥3 independent conditioned-medium lots, (1) spike-in tracer is recovered in capture-positive particle-peak fractions and loses signal after detergent+protease (assay validated), and (2) endogenous capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive anti-inflammatory activity are reproducibly observed in the bounded fraction but not in secretome-retaining concentrates processed identically. This pattern enables a pass/fail identity+potency gate (bounded fraction = EV-enriched pass; secretome = fail).

explicit_inferences: Inference: Spike-in recovery that is membrane-protected validates assay sensitivity for intact EVs and allows interpretation of endogenous capture co-localization.
Inference: Loss of activity after detergent+protease in capture-positive fractions supports that activity is membrane-protected (EV-associated) rather than soluble.
falsification_criteria: Validated spike-in recovery (membrane-protected) but no reproducible endogenous capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks in bounded fractions across independent lots (n ≥ 3), OR
Spike-in-validated capture-positive fractions show no detergent/protease-sensitive loss of endogenous activity (i.e., activity is detergent-insensitive), OR
Secretome-retaining fractions show equivalent, detergent-sensitive activity co-localized with particle peaks, preventing discrimination.
human_decisions_required: Select exact bounded fractionation workflow (TFF->SEC vs SEC+cushion vs capture-enrichment) and spike-in tracer format
Approve microglia in vitro assay platform and endpoints to be used as the functional readout
Decide sample size (number of independent lots) and replication strategy for qualitative replication
manufacturability_assessment: The experiment uses a minimal, production-relevant fractionation (e.g., TFF concentration followed by SEC or a single-cushion iodixanol step) and an exogenous spike-in to control assay recovery; if supported, the bounded fraction strategy is compatible with downstream QC and early GMP-like batch considerations (yield must be assessed qualitatively).
manufacturing_rationale: A qualitative, spike-in‑controlled fraction-level pass/fail gate enables an early manufacturability decision: only preparations that reproducibly pass this gate should be pursued as bounded EV drug‑substance candidates for CMC, potency assay development, and scale-up; failing materials will be treated as secretome products or require alternate fractionation.
measurement_strategy: Orthogonal fraction-level workflow with per-sample spike-in (exogenous intact EV tracer) + particle counting (NTA/TRPS) per fraction + intact immuno-capture readout distinguishing spike-in vs endogenous marker + detergent+protease protection assay + fraction eluate in vitro microglia LPS cytokine assay + total protein and protein:particle context. Qualitative pass/fail rules define identity+potency gate; numeric release criteria deferred until assay validation.
novelty_statement: This hypothesis specifies a new, spike-in–controlled fraction-level discriminating experiment that explicitly links membrane-protection (spike-in validation + detergent/protease sensitivity), particle:marker co-localization, and a standardized in vitro neuroinflammation readout to distinguish EV-associated activity from non-EV secretome contributions. It differs from prior proposals by combining a per-sample exogenous intact‑EV tracer (to validate recovery and exclude assay failure) with fraction‑level protection testing and a matched functional assay applied to capture‑eluates — an integrated discriminating experiment not previously proposed in SGL‑001 materials.
principal_risks: Assay artifacts (capture-reagent incompatibility or spike-in failure) could misclassify materials.
Even if EV-associated activity is demonstrated in vitro, intranasal delivery barriers in larger species may still prevent in vivo translation.
Material yield from bounded fraction may be insufficient for manufacturing-scale decisions; yield assessment is required.
proposed_potency_relationship: If the protected fraction reproducibly carries detergent/protease-sensitive anti-inflammatory activity in vitro, that activity becomes the candidate mechanism-linked potency attribute for gating EV-enriched drug‑substance advancement (qualitative linkage only).
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: If supported, adopt a pass/fail identity+potency gate defined as: a spike-in–validated, membrane-protected, capture-positive particle fraction that (A) co-localizes capture-positive signal with particle-count peaks, (B) shows detergent+protease-sensitive protected cargo and (C) contains an in vitro neuroinflammation‑modulating activity abolished by membrane disruption — to classify an EV-enriched bounded small-EV drug-substance candidate versus secretome-like material (non-numeric, qualitative gate).
title: Spike-in–controlled fraction-level protected-bioactivity test to discriminate EV-associated vs non-EV secretome contributions (SGL-001)
